answer.note: Each file has one sample column of whole numbers per Ensembl gene (e.g. 410, 0, 1000, 1), with many zeros and differing totals, which fits raw read counts rather than normalised values. All four samples are given, each identified by the column name matching its file and accession.

Each file is featureCounts v2.0.0 output (Ensembl gene IDs in column 1, integer counts in column 7, file names say raw_readcounts), so these are raw read counts. The 12 files map one-to-one to Samples 1–12 by file number and by timepoint_N_R matching the sample's Age N and Replicate R; all samples are given.

Each GSM3095576–599 member of the tar is a headerless two-column Rsubread counts file (NCBI gene ID, whole-number count, many zeros), so the values are raw read counts. All 24 samples are given; the ChIP-seq peak and bedgraph members belong to other GSM accessions and hold no gene counts.

Columns 7-12 hold whole-number values (e.g. 419, 193, 269) that differ from the separate CPM columns 13-18, so they are raw counts per Ensembl gene. All six samples are given, matched through the replicate IDs in the sample titles (G400_1_1 etc.).

The file is named read counts and holds small whole-number values (0, 1, 2) per Ensembl gene, consistent with raw counts. All 16 samples are given, matched by the titles in the header row (EV_49 to shAHCY4_64).

The files are gene count matrices (columns such as A01_count) with mostly integer values and some fractional ones (e.g. 2015.39), which look like expected counts from RSEM-style quantification rather than normalised values such as FPKM or TPM. All 12 samples are given, matched via the well codes (A01–A03, B01–B03, H01–H03, I01–I03) in the sample descriptions.

The file has Ensembl gene IDs with whole-number values (e.g. 833, 942, 0) per column, so these are raw read counts. All 10 samples are given: column names (ctr/RAS, siCTR/siMETTL3 vec/WT/MT, replicate number) match the sample titles; I did not check the counts against the sample records, since only the file description was available.

The columns are named "*_count" in "gene.count.matrix" files and hold unscaled per-gene counts, many of them whole numbers (0, 5, 9, 544). Some are fractional (e.g. 2015.39), which suggests expected counts from a quantifier such as RSEM, not normalised values; the sample columns (A01–C03) map to the GSMs through the titles. All nine samples are given.

GSE162175_Rawcounts.txt.gz has Ensembl gene IDs with whole-number, widely varying values (e.g. 1, 29434), as expected for raw counts. All 32 samples are matched to columns by the sample names in the header (e.g. IMR90_Control_1 is GSM4944235, IMR90_iRas_pos_1 is GSM4944263).

Each workbook has per-sample "_count" columns holding small whole numbers (0, 1, 2, 7), separate from the "_tpm" columns with decimals, so the counts are raw. All 12 samples are given, each from its own file's columns 5-7, matched by column names.

Columns named D1.rawreads ... M3.rawreads hold whole-number values (separate from the FPKM columns), so they are raw read counts per Ensembl gene. The sample mapping follows the sample titles ([D1]-[D3] = DMSO, [M1]-[M3] = mitoxantrone); all six samples are given, but the file only lists the significant DE genes, not every gene.

The columns named D1–D3 and M1–M3 ".rawreads" hold whole-number counts, next to separate FPKM columns. Sample titles give the mapping D1–D3 to the DMSO samples and M1–M3 to the mitoxantrone samples. All six samples are given, but the file lists only the significant differentially expressed genes, not every gene.

Each workbook has whole-number "*_count" columns (5–7) alongside separate "*_tpm" columns (8–10) with Ensembl gene IDs in column 1, so the count columns are raw read counts. The column names are A01–A03, B01–B03 and C01–C03 rather than sample names, so I assigned them by inference: file A to CTRL, B to BLEO and C to RAD, taking the file letters to follow the CTRL, BLEO, RAD order and matching the numbers 01–03. Treat that assignment as likely but not confirmed.

The "Expected count" columns are RSEM expected read counts, which are estimated counts and not scaled. They are separate from the TPM and FPKM columns, but some values are fractional (e.g. 78.57), so they are not strictly whole numbers. The samples map by the column labels: Y is GSM5901576, S is GSM5901577, and S-C (S+C) is GSM5901578. All three samples are given.

The count file holds whole-number values per Ensembl gene (e.g. 0, 1, 2, 6, 7), while the companion file is TPM with decimals. Columns w1–z5 are matched to samples through the sample titles (UJ-3100-w1 etc.); all 20 samples are given, and the TPM file is left out as normalised.

Each tar member is a per-sample file ("CountsData") with Ensembl gene IDs and whole-number values, including many zeros and small integers, so they are raw counts. The column header in each member matches the sample title, and all 12 samples are given.

Each file has per-sample "_count" columns, separate from the "_tpm" columns. Most values are whole numbers, and a few are fractional (e.g. 2.35, 5.97), which suggests RSEM-style expected counts, not normalised values. All 24 samples are given, matched by the sample names in the column headers (HBF_, huc_, HUVE_, IMR_ with C01–C03 and B01–B03).

The file is named as raw gene counts and holds whole numbers (e.g. 0, 1, 117, 132) per NCBI gene ID. All eight samples are given, matched by the column names, which are the sample descriptions (PRO-WT-1 and so on).

The three *_all_genome_counts.txt.gz files hold whole-number counts per Ensembl gene (ENSG) with sample-named columns, matched to samples via the sample descriptions. GSM6995000–GSM6995011 are not given: the DESeq2 results file holds only statistics, and their tar members hold per-transcript (ENST) counts, not per-gene counts.

The three gene_count_matrix files hold whole-number, unscaled per-gene values (0, 3, 33251, ...), consistent with raw counts. All 21 samples are given; the ABR1-ABR3 columns of the Senescence file are not listed again because those samples are already given from the FOXO3Act file. The F3KD columns are matched to samples by the names shControlRNA1-3 and shFOXO3RNA1-3 and the replicate numbers in the sample titles.

Each tar member is a featureCounts output (v1.6.3, hg19.refGene.gtf) with integer counts in column 7 (e.g. 0) per gene symbol, which are raw read counts. All 8 samples are given; each member is named after its sample.

The files hold whole-number per-gene counts with Ensembl gene IDs, and two carry featureCounts headers, so they are raw read counts. All 70 samples are in the sources. In the IMR90 shHMGA1 file the BAM names are matched by inference: Sh_G = GrowshA1, Sh_S = RISshA1, V_G = Grow, V_S = RIS, each numbered 1 to 8. In the shCEBPB_shp53 file the header row has no name for column 1, so each name sits one column to its right.

Each tar member is a featureCounts output (Geneid, Chr, Start, End, Strand, Length, then one count column) with integer values per Ensembl gene, so these are raw read counts. All 24 samples are given, one member per sample, each with its GSM accession in the member name.

GSE248979_rawcounts.txt.gz has whole-number values in columns named *_count (e.g. 251417, 277327) per Ensembl gene, while the FPKM file holds normalised decimals. All six samples are given, matched by column names (DMF_1-3 = DMF rep1-3, Cis_1-3 = Cisplatin rep1-3); the file's remaining columns (8-41) were not shown and are not assigned to any sample.

The file is named a raw count matrix and holds whole-number values per Ensembl gene. The header row has no name for column 1, so the 10 names (B1-NR to B6-IR) sit over columns 2-11. These names match the sample descriptions, so all 10 samples are given.
The HTSeq counts file holds small whole-number values per gene symbol (0, 1, 4, 3, 2), consistent with raw counts. Column names match the sample titles (NPC-1-NC etc.), so all six samples are given.

The count table has Ensembl gene IDs with whole-number values per sample (e.g. 540288, 13294), consistent with raw counts. The column names are the sample descriptions (e.g. C_CTL_3), which match the samples' description fields, so all 18 samples are given.

GSE259291_gene_count.tsv.gz holds whole-number values (many 0) per Ensembl gene, which indicates raw counts. The FPKM file is normalised and not used. All 12 samples are given, matched by column names (e.g. pEV1 to description pEV_1).

GSE259295_gene_count.tsv.gz holds whole-number per-gene counts (e.g. 170, 65, 94) for all 18 samples, with column names matching the sample descriptions (Prolif_DMSO_1 etc.); the fpkm file is normalised and not used. All samples are given.

Columns 11-16 are named "_count" and hold whole numbers (e.g. 11, 6, 14, 818), unlike the non-integer FPKM values in columns 5-10. All six samples are given, matched by the sample names in the column headers.

The file is named raw_counts and holds whole-number values per Ensembl gene (e.g. 417, 563, 0), consistent with raw read counts. All 16 samples are given, matched by the column names, which equal the sample titles.

The Raw_Gene_Counts_Matrix holds mostly whole-number counts per gene (e.g. 1382, 539), unlike the FPKM matrix with small decimals; a few entries are fractional (e.g. 27.02, 40.71), probably from the quantification tool's estimated counts, so I took them as counts. All 12 samples are given, matched to columns by the column names, which equal the sample titles; the FPKM matrix is normalised and left out.

Each tar member is a per-sample table of Uniprot IDs with small whole-number values (e.g. 3, 8, 0, 12), consistent with raw read counts and not normalised values. All 12 samples are given, each matched by its GSM accession in the member name.

Both files have whole-number "_count" columns per sample, separate from the "_tpm" columns (e.g. a count of 3 matches a TPM of 0.4), so these are raw counts. The BLEO-01..03 count columns in the BP_vs_BLE file repeat samples GSM8215990–92, which are already given from the BLE_vs_CTR file, so they are left out.

The matrix holds whole-number values per gene symbol (e.g. TSPAN6 152, 28, 187), consistent with raw read counts. All eight samples are given; columns A549_1 to A549_8 match the numeric suffixes in the sample titles.

The counts file ("ft_counts", featureCounts) holds whole-number, unscaled values per gene (NCBI gene IDs in column 1), with columns named qui1-3, pro1-3 and sen1-3. These map to the titles of the quiescent, proliferating and senescent replicates. The other two files are differential-expression results (logFC, FDR), not counts. All nine samples are given.
Each tar member is a featureCounts output (v2.0.1, exon-level, gene_id) with whole-number counts in column 7 (e.g. 1, 47, 75) per Ensembl gene ID. All nine samples are given, one member each.

Each tar member is a headerless two-column file of Ensembl gene IDs and whole-number values, named "exon.counts", with a different value per sample (e.g. 288, 790, 131), which fits raw read counts. All 12 samples are given, each matched by the GSM accession in its member name.

Although the file name says "tpm", the values shown are whole numbers (e.g. A1BG 21, 22, 25; A1CF 0 or 1), which fits raw counts and not TPM, so they are treated as raw counts; this is uncertain because of the file name. All 18 samples are given, matched through the sample description codes (e.g. D01IPS = GSM8365514) that are the column names.

Columns 3-14 of the combined GENCODE file hold whole-number values (e.g. 455, 426, 537 for BAK1), while the columns named .CPM and .TPM hold decimal normalised values. All 12 samples are given, matched by the column names to the sample descriptions. The RAW tar holds only sample sheets, with no counts.

Each tar member is a featureCounts output (Geneid, Chr, Start, End, Strand, Length, then a count column) with whole-number values per Ensembl gene, so these are raw read counts. All 24 samples are given, each matched to its member by GSM accession in the file name.

The *_count columns are per-gene read counts (some non-integer, e.g. 2.75, so they look like RSEM-style estimated counts), kept separate from the *_tpm columns, which are the normalised values. The BLEO columns in the second file are not listed because those samples are already given from the first file.

The file is named a raw gene counts matrix and holds whole-number values per gene (e.g. 99, 87, 0, 1, 4). Columns A9_1–3 and NC_1–3 map to the samples via their descriptions (A9_n = OE-n, NC_n = NC-n), so all six samples are given.

The file has whole-number values per Ensembl gene in columns named after each sample's BAM file (featureCounts-style), which indicates raw read counts. All 12 samples are given, matched through the sample descriptions, which match the column names.

The readcount file is a STAR per-gene count table with integer values (N_unmapped, N_multimapping, N_noFeature summary rows, as in STAR ReadsPerGene output); the TPM file holds normalised values and is not used. The gene rows are not shown, so first_values_row 6 is inferred (the STAR N_ambiguous row is presumably row 5); all nine samples are given, matched through the column names, which are the sample descriptions.

The files are named ".counts" and hold whole-number values per Ensembl gene (many zeros, varying integers), consistent with raw read counts. All 18 samples are matched by column names to their titles, so none are left out.

Each tar member is a per-sample TEtranscripts-style cntTable (gene/TE header, Ensembl gene IDs) holding whole-number counts from hisat2 BAMs, including zeros, so they are raw read counts. All 17 samples are given, each identified by its GSM accession in the member name.

Each tar member is a headerless two-column table: an Ensembl gene ID in column 1 and a whole-number count in column 2 (e.g. 1, 139, 7, 0). The file names say "countGenes". All 36 samples are given, one member each, matched by the GSM accession in the member name.

The featureCounts output has integer values per gene symbol, with one BAM-named column per sample, so these are raw counts. Columns map to samples through the sample descriptions (Nor_Ctrl_2 etc.); all 8 samples are given.

GSE279411_raw_counts.txt.gz holds whole-number values per Ensembl gene (e.g. 0, 1, 48, 90) for all 12 samples; columns were matched to samples by the names (Prolif/IR/IR.CTPI2/IR.UK with replicate numbers 1-3). The TPM file was not read and is not used; all samples are given.

Each tar member is a per-sample HTSeq count file (no header) with gene symbol in column 1 and whole-number counts in column 2, e.g. A1BG 608; the member names carry the sample accessions. All 15 samples are given in sources.

Each per-sample RSEM genes.results file has an expected_count column (column 5) with whole-number values (e.g. 1367.00, 0.00), next to separate TPM and FPKM columns, so column 5 is the unnormalised count. All 42 samples are given, each identified by the GSM accession in its member name.

The readcount file holds whole-number values per Ensembl gene (e.g. 430, 426, 328), whereas the FPKM file holds decimals and is normalised. All six samples are given, mapped by the column names shC_1–3 and shPML_1–3, which match the sample titles.

Each per-sample tab-delimited member has no header, a gene symbol in columns 1 and 2, and whole-number values in column 3 (e.g. 245, 0, 5940), which are raw counts. Samples were matched by the GSM accession in the member name; the file labels for GSM8328993–96 (siBANF1 / siSRRM2) are swapped relative to the sample titles, but the accession identifies the file. The other members (bigWig and narrowPeak files) are not gene counts.

Each tar member is a per-sample tab-delimited file named *_geneCOUNT with Ensembl gene IDs in column 1 and whole-number counts in column 2 (e.g. 6291, 0, 4733). The sample accession is in each member name, and all 190 samples are given.

Each tar member is a featureCounts v2.0.3 output (exon-level, gene_id summarised) with a header row 2 and an integer count in column 7, such as 0 for DDX11L1. These are unnormalised counts. All 60 samples are given, one member each, named by its GSM accession.
The featureCounts table holds whole-number counts per Ensembl gene, and its column names (library names such as 1_S1) match the sample descriptions. All 16 samples are given in sources.

The matrix holds whole-number, unscaled values per Ensembl gene (e.g. 1836, 2, 0), which are raw counts. The header row has 45 names and the data rows have 46 fields, so column 1 is the gene ID and each name sits one column to the right. Names are the library names, which match the sample descriptions, so all 45 samples are given.

Each per-sample tar member has gene symbols in column 1 and whole-number values in column 2 (e.g. PEX10 984, RPL21P21 0), with no header, consistent with raw counts. Row 1 has no gene name, so gene rows start at row 2. In five members, column 3 is a constant per-gene value (likely gene length), not counts. All 17 samples are given.

GSE289427_counts.sf_raw.txt.gz holds whole-number gene counts per Ensembl gene. The sf_norm file holds decimal size-factor-normalised values, so it is not used. Samples were matched to columns through the library names (M_x) in the sample descriptions, and all 22 samples are given.

The file is named counts and holds whole-number values (zeros for unexpressed genes) per Ensembl_symbol gene row, consistent with raw read counts. All 18 samples are given; each column name is the library name from the sample description (the column 8 name has a trailing space).

Each member is an RSEM genes.results file whose expected_count column (5) holds per-gene estimated read counts, in the same files as the TPM and FPKM columns. The values are mostly non-integer (e.g. 242.84) because RSEM estimates them. All 18 samples are given, one member each.

Columns RNA_QL1_count to RNA_QL4_count hold whole numbers per Ensembl gene, next to separate FPKM columns, so they are raw counts. The sample library names (RNA_QL1–4) match the column names, so all four samples are given.

The file has Ensembl gene IDs with whole-number values (many zeros, e.g. 421, 1020), which are raw counts. The header row has one field fewer than the data rows, so its names start at column 2. Samples are matched through the library names (s_..._z for passages 20, s_..._m for passages 12), and all 36 samples are given.

Each tar member is a per-sample HTSeq output with Ensembl gene IDs in column 1 and whole-number counts in column 2, with no header row. Values such as 619, 361 and 0 are integers and differ between samples. All 42 samples are given, each identified by its GSM accession in the member name.

The STAR gene counts file holds whole-number, mostly small values (many 0s, 1, 2), consistent with raw counts. All 12 samples are given, matched through the library names (H_CNT_1 is GSM8898773 and H_CNT_2 is GSM8898772, as their library names say).

The matrix holds whole-number values per gene symbol (e.g. 22, 114, 0, 1), consistent with raw read counts despite the 'Processed' file name. The columns "Sample 1" to "Sample 15" map to the samples through the library names in the sample descriptions, and all 15 samples are given.

The file is named raw gene counts and the shown values are whole numbers (0) per Ensembl gene. Column headers are library names (PU01001 etc.) that match the sample descriptions' "Library name", so all nine samples are given.
The file is named raw gene counts and holds whole-number values per Ensembl gene (e.g. 1302604 for FN1). All 15 samples are matched by title to the column names, so all are given.

Columns count.Con1–count.OE3 hold whole-number values (e.g. 1595, 3228) alongside separate non-integer FPKM columns, so they are raw read counts; the sample titles match the column suffixes. All six samples are given.

The STAR ReadsPerGene.out.tab members in the tar hold integer per-gene read counts (column 2 is the unstranded count, as the sample descriptions say). Rows 1-4 are the N_unmapped, N_multimapping, N_noFeature and N_ambiguous summary lines, and I took gene rows to start at row 5 (not shown). Not given: GSM9844043-51 are in the MCF7 counts matrix, but its header has 9 names and each data row has only 8 values after the gene ID, so the columns can't be matched to samples. The LS8817 samples GSM8944501-19 have kallisto transcript-level est_counts (non-integer) and a DESeq2-normalised matrix, so they have no raw per-gene counts.

The merged_gene_count file holds whole-number per-gene values (Ensembl IDs), while the rpkm file holds non-integer RPKM values. All nine samples are given, matched by column names (Ctrl_1_R, Ctrl_2, Ctrl_3, SR_1-3, Sen_1-3) to the sample titles.

The file is featureCounts v2.0.3 output (with --countReadPairs) with small whole-number values per Ensembl gene, so these are raw read counts. All 21 samples are given; library names in the sample descriptions match the column headers, and 4Gamma_3 (column 23) comes before 4Gamma_2 (column 24) in the file.

Each tar member is a headerless two-column file of Ensembl gene IDs and whole-number values (e.g. 139, 0, 972) in files named "_counts.txt", which fits raw read counts. All 18 samples are given, each matched to its member by its GSM accession.

The file is named raw_counts and has integer values per Ensembl gene (featureCounts-style layout with Geneid, Chr, Start, End, Strand, Length columns). All 21 samples are matched to columns by the column names (e.g. BJ_P11_DOX_50ngml_rep1 maps to GSM9076621).
The values are whole numbers per Ensembl gene (e.g. 16, 11, 0), consistent with raw read counts. All 11 samples are matched by column names, which are the sample titles.

The file is named "Count" and holds whole-number values per gene symbol, many zeros and small integers, so these are raw counts. All 24 samples are mapped through the library name (e.g. GBM12.1 = column GBM12-1); columns GBM12-9 and GBM28-9 match no sample and are left out.

The readcount file holds whole-number values per Ensembl gene (e.g. 1697, 2885, 0), unlike the FPKM file with decimals. MG_1–5 match MG1–5 by name; HG_1–5 are mapped to HG_A–E (A=1 … E=5), which is also the order of the library numbers 6–10, so that mapping is an inference from letter/number correspondence.

Both files hold small whole-number values per Ensembl gene (many zeros, 1, 2, 4), and the file names say rawcounts, so these are raw read counts. All 14 samples are given; column names (CT-1..4, V-1..3 and CT1-1..4, V1-1..3) match the library names in the sample descriptions (CT_1.., V_1.., CT1_1.., V1_1..).

GeneMat_Count_all holds per-gene "count" columns (f1–f12, mapped to the samples by their descriptions). Many values are integers and the rest are fractional with two decimals, which suggests estimated counts such as RSEM expected counts, not scaled values. They differ from the TPM file, whose values are small and normalised. The TPM file is not a source. All 12 samples are given.

GSE306839_raw_counts.csv.gz holds whole-number per-gene Ensembl counts that match the featureCounts values in the per-sample tar members, whereas the TPM file holds decimals. Samples map to columns via library names SV19–SV36 (description field, confirmed by the tar member names); all 18 samples are given, and the tar members duplicate the same counts so they are left out.

The file is a count matrix with whole-number values per gene (many zeros, values like 107, 91, 129), consistent with raw read counts. All 18 samples are given, matched by the sample titles in the column names (P#_State_Treatment).
The file is named raw counts and holds whole-number values per Ensembl gene, including many small values like 0 and 2. Column names "Passage N" match the sample titles, so all 9 samples are given.

The file has columns named "..._Read_Count" holding whole numbers (e.g. 38, 408, 0) per NCBI Gene_ID, so they are raw counts. All 60 samples are mapped by the column names given in their descriptions. The R2 day-7 AGL columns (56–63) have a double underscore in the header (e.g. "A549_D7_AGL__CT_R2"), but they still match their samples.

Values are whole numbers (e.g. 365, 580, 0) per Ensembl gene, and the sample descriptions say counts were generated by featureCounts, so they are raw counts. All six samples are given, matched by the column names ZL34_GFP1..3 and ZL34_PTPA1..3 to the sample titles.

The count matrix is featureCounts output (header comment, integer values such as 32, 38, 58 per gene), so it holds raw read counts; columns are matched to samples by the column names given in the sample descriptions. The TPM file holds normalised values and is not used. All nine samples are given.

The file is named gene_count and holds whole-number values per Ensembl gene (e.g. 433034 for FN1), consistent with raw counts. Column headers are the library names given in the sample descriptions (QM1 to SV4ac), so all 32 samples are mapped.

Columns 28-39 are named read_count_<sample> and hold per-gene counts (mostly whole numbers, some with decimals such as 668.68, so probably estimated/expected counts) next to separate FPKM and TPM columns. Only the replicate-1 samples are listed, since their column names (…1A) match the library names; replicates 2 and 3 are left out because the columns are labelled 3A and 4A, which cannot be matched to rep2 and rep3 from the names.

Columns bal_001_count to bal_016_count hold whole-number values per Ensembl gene (separate from the FPKM and normalised/DE columns), so they are raw counts. Samples GSM9421160–GSM9421171 (bal_017–bal_028) are not in the file, which only has bal_001–bal_016.

GSE316481_counts.txt.gz holds whole-number per-gene values (Ensembl IDs, including zeros) for all six samples, which are raw read counts; the variance-stabilised file holds transformed non-integer values and is not used. All samples are given, matched by the column names (control 1-3, miR-205-5p 1-3) to the sample titles.

GSE319937_raw_counts.csv.gz holds whole-number values per Ensembl gene (e.g. 0, 1, 150, 129), unlike the decimal TPM file; columns are matched to samples by the library names (e.g. Prol.1 = GSM9529720) in the header. All 18 samples are given.

Values are whole numbers per Ensembl gene (including zeros) in files named "all_gene_counts", so they are raw read counts. All 23 samples are given; GSM9566097 is matched to the column headed "rara4_sum" (a typo for rapa4_sum, sitting between rapa3 and rapa5).

The sheet "allsamples.count" holds whole-number values per gene symbol (e.g. WASH7P 223, 286, 227), many zeros, which indicates raw counts. Columns are matched to samples by the library names in the sample descriptions (Control_1 to shMTR4_3); all six samples are given.

The values are non-negative whole numbers (e.g. 835, 0, 1081) in a file named "counts", with Ensembl gene IDs as rows, so they are raw read counts. Columns are named "Sample NNNN" and matched to GSM accessions through the "Library name: Sample NNNN" descriptions; 10 samples (0010, 0135, 0136, 0143, 0144, 0211, 0212, 0219, 0220, 0235) have no column in the file and are not given.

The sheet is named a gene count matrix and its values are whole numbers (0, 3, 11) per gene symbol, consistent with raw counts. All six samples are given, matched by the column names HDF-NC1..3 and HDF-UVA1..3 to the sample titles NC1..3 and UVA1..3.

The nf-core salmon merged gene_counts table (Ensembl gene IDs) holds estimated read counts per gene; many values are integers or near-integers (e.g. 0, 1, 138.999, 216.027) and are not scaled like TPM or CPM. Every sample is mapped to its column through the library name in its description, which matches the column header; the h5 files in the RAW tar are single-cell matrices belonging to other GSM accessions, so they are not used.
The file gene_counts.tsv holds whole-number values (0 and 1) per Ensembl gene, consistent with raw counts. All 24 samples are matched by the column names given in each sample description.

Each tar member is a per-sample table of Ensembl gene IDs with whole-number values (e.g. 2, 146, 2642), including zeros and small counts, which indicates raw counts rather than normalised values. All 12 samples are given, each in its own member.

The file holds tximport estimated counts per gene (Ensembl IDs); many values are whole numbers and the rest are non-integer expected counts (e.g. 1016.93), not scaled or transformed values like TPM or FPKM, so I treated them as raw read counts. All 27 samples are given, matched by the column names (the library names in each sample's description).

The raw_counts file holds whole-number values per gene symbol (e.g. 0, 1, 3, 5), while the normalized_counts file holds fractional values for the same genes. All 30 samples are given, matched by the library names in the column headers to the sample descriptions.

The file gives whole-number fragment counts per Ensembl gene (many zeros, varying integer values), so they are raw counts, not normalised. All 14 samples are matched by library name to columns; columns 14 and 15 (HFCK7DSXY ...R, the earlier runs of 003 and 005) match no sample and are left out.
